newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish SLD keeps lead in first poll after flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish SLD keeps lead in first poll after flood.

text.p: Poland's first opinion poll since the start of this month's heavy flooding showed the co-ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) keeping its top spot, private Radio Zet said on Friday.

It said the poll, conducted from July 10 to 20 by the public CBOS institute for Radio Zet and the Gazeta Wyborcza daily, showed the ex-communist SLD with 26 percent support ahead of the Solidarity-led AWS alliance, backed by 22 percent.

But a CBOS sociologist said most of the polling was carried out from July 10 to 12 when the public was not yet fully aware of the scope of the disaster and before a heated parliamentary debate over the government's handling of the crisis.

"Usually about 80 percent of the polling is done in the first two days and on July 10-12 people knew that there was a flood but were unaware that it was such a cataclysm, a deluge," Andrzej Mokrzyszewski told Radio Zet.

He also said the poll showed that the floods, which swamped 6,000 square km and more than one thousand villages and towns, killing 55 people, had a bigger negative effect on the government's approval ratings than on voter preferences.
Other institutes delayed their polling because of the floods and new results are expected early next month.

NOTE - Party names:
AWS - The Solidarity Electoral Action, an opposition electoral bloc of more than 30 small right-wing parties led by the Solidarity trade union.
SLD - the Democratic Left Alliance, the ex-communist group and the larger partner in the ruling leftist coalition.
PSL - The Polish the smaller partner in the government coalition.
UW - The Union for Freedom, a right-centrist group, the biggest opposition party in parliament.
ROP - The Movement for Reconstruction of Poland, a non-parliamentary group, advocating patriotic, anti-communist and often populist values.
UP - The Union of Labour, a leftist opposition party.
KPEiR - The National Pensioners' Party, a party lobbying pensioners' interests.
Polling agencies:
CBOS - public, Poland's biggest polling institution. OBOP - controlled by the state-owned television.
DEMOSKOP - private.
PBS - private, preparing polls for the Rzeczpospolita daily. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
